A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PureCC paper and complete supplementary material, including Sections 8–16. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable and directly matchable; differences are confined to the version stamp and Figure 3 with nearby layout shifts.

before.justification: v1 reports original customization experiments, quantitative comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–3, supplementary analyses, and a 42-participant user study with results in Table 7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, supplementary analyses and user-study outcomes.

M1.justification: Figure 3(b) removes the flame/trainability icon beside the concept embeddings feeding the second-stage trainable model. Sections 4.2–4.4, the equations and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects the diagram or changes the intended embedding-training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 30-concept qualitative collection and DreamBenchPCC extension with 12 style concepts. Single-concept, multi-concept and style–instance customization coverage remains identical, including supplementary examples.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DreamBooth, DreamBooth+EWC, Mix-of-Show, CIFC, DreamO and UNO. LoRA, LoRA-S and B-LoRA also remain in their corresponding comparisons; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The explicitly stated evaluation settings remain identical: SD 3.5-M, the same metrics, 400 training steps per stage, 28 inference timesteps and the same 42-participant user-study design. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The loss and training-stage ablations, guidance-scale tests, eta sensitivity analysis, learning-process visualizations and comparison of original-prediction sources are unchanged, including Tables 2, 3 and 6 and Figure 16.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the same point estimates and user-preference percentages are retained.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and all empirical figures retain the same results and examples. For instance, Table 1 reports PureCC instance CLIP-I of 0.81 and Seg-Cons of 69.37 in both versions; Table 7's preference percentages are also identical.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(15), the representation definitions and the projection-based derivation of the adaptive guidance scale in Equations (11)–(12) are unchanged. No formal assumption, proof or mathematical result is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about the decoupled objective, dual-branch pipeline, adaptive guidance and preservation of original-model behavior while achieving concept fidelity.

C2.justification: Interpretations of preservation–fidelity tradeoffs, insufficient guidance under merged training, hyperparameter sensitivity and computational overhead remain unchanged. No new applicability boundary or limitation is stated.

D1.justification: Removing the flame icon beside the second-stage embeddings in Figure 3(b) changes the visual documentation of trainability, without an accompanying explanation. Written hyperparameters, hardware, resource costs, inference instructions and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning statements and all 54 references are unchanged. No cited work or relationship to prior research is added or removed.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 8 March 2026 to v2 dated 19 May 2026. The paper's prose, captions, terminology and section structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is slightly rearranged and removes the flame icon beside the second-stage embeddings, with small shifts in the surrounding page layout. Its caption, all tables and the remaining figures, including supplementary figures, are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, experimental evidence and complete supplement are unchanged. The only potentially consequential edit removes an embedding-trainability cue in Figure 3(b), without explaining whether it corrects an error or removes accurate guidance. Its effect on reproducibility, and therefore any overall quality gain or loss, remains unresolved.
